summary: Valeria Gazizova is a scholar in tibetology and religious studies who prepared her master's thesis at the University of Oslo, studying under Hanna Havnevik and Per Kværne.

Valerie Hansen is a historian and sinologist who studied at Harvard University (~1975–1979) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1981–1987) under Victor H. Mair. She taught at Yale University (~1993–1998) and East China Normal University (2005).

Valerie Stoker works in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, and holds a post at Wright State University. She received traditional instruction under D. Prahladachar and Krishnacharya Tammannacharya Pandurangi.

Valery Evgenyevich Krasnodembsky (1907–1942) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Leningrad Oriental Institute (~1926–1930). He later worked there (1932–1942), at the Institute of Ethnography (1933–1937), and taught at Saint Petersburg State University (1934–1942).
Vamana was an Indologist who studied under traditional teachers Keshava, Dattatreya Sastri Nigudkar, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.
Vamanshastri Kinjawadekar was a scholar of Indology and philosophy who studied under traditional teachers Dattatreya, Virupaksha, and Vaidyanatha.

Van Austin Harvey (1926–2021) was a religious studies scholar and philosopher educated at Occidental College, Princeton Theological Seminary, and Yale University. He held positions at Princeton, Southern Methodist University, the University of Pennsylvania, and Stanford University (~1978–1996).
Vandita Srivastava is a scholar in Indology and linguistics who completed a Bachelor of Arts (Hons.) (2004–2007) and a Ph.D. (2010–2016) at Banaras Hindu University.

Vans Kennedy (1784–1846) was an Indologist and linguist. He served as judge-advocate-general in the Bombay Army (1817–1835) and was an active member and later President (1831–1835) of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai.

Vasant Shinde is a scholar of archaeology and Indology who served as Professor and Professor of South Asian Archaeology at the Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 2006, 2026).

Vasile Burlă (1840–1905) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied at the universities of Vienna (~1864–1867) and Graz (~1867–1870). He served as a university lecturer in Classics at Alexandru Ioan Cuza University (~1872–1901).

Vasilij Alekseevič Bogorodickij (1857–1941) was a linguist who studied under Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay at Kazan State University (~1876–1880). He held docent and professor positions at Kazan State University (1881–1893) and Kazan State Pedagogical University (1922–1925).

Vasilij Alekseevič Bogoslovskij (1932–1986) was a scholar of Tibetology, Sinology, and history who studied at Moscow State University (~1949–1954). He held posts at the University of Chicago (1957–1967) and the Institute of China and Contemporary Asia (1968).

Vasilij Ivanovič Smirnov (b. 1898) was an Indologist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies and under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov at Saint Petersburg State University (~1928–1932). He was a docent at Leningrad Oriental Institute (1936–1937).

Vasilij Matveevič Beskrovnyj (1908–1978) was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Aleksej Petrovič Barannikov at Leningrad Oriental Institute. He worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts and taught at Saint Petersburg State University and Moscow State University.

Vasilij Vasil'evič Brodov (1912–1996) was a philosopher and Indologist educated at Moscow Institute of Philosophy, Literature and History. He held teaching and research posts at institutions including the Institute of Philosophy, Moscow State University, and All-Union Correspondence Civil Engineering Institute.

Vasily Mikhaylovich Alekseyev (1881–1951) was a sinologist who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Édouard Chavannes. He held posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1909–1951), the Institute of Oriental Studies (~1918–1951), and the National Library of Russia.

Vasily Pavlovich Vasilyev (1818–1900) was a sinologist and Tibetologist who studied at Kazan State University under Franz von Erdmann and Józef Szczepan Kowalewski. He served as professor at Kazan State University and Saint Petersburg State University (1855–1893).

Vasily Radlov (1837–1918) was a linguist and historian who studied at Berlin and Jena under August Friedrich Pott and Wilhelm Schott. He directed the Asiatic Museum (1885–1890) and the Peter the Great Museum of Anthropology and Ethnography (1894–1918).

Vasily Seseman (1884–1963) was a philosopher who studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1903–1909). He held academic posts at Saint Petersburg State University (~1915–1918), Vytautas Magnus University (~1923–1939), and Vilnius University (~1939–1950).
